brand.name: OH SNAP
brand.positioning: A high-speed Tucson smoothie concept built around fruit-forward flavor, protein options, local desert signatures and a very small food layer.
brand.working_name_status: Working brand — trademark and legal clearance required before major spend

strategic_verdict.launch_format: Paid pop-up or trailer first; second-generation end-cap next; raw-land purchase last
strategic_verdict.first_test_zone: Golf Links Road at or near Kolb Road
strategic_verdict.second_test_zone: Speedway Boulevard at or near Kolb Road
strategic_verdict.land_rule: Do not buy raw land just because it is under $200,000. The site must also support commercial use, access, stacking, utilities and the full project budget.
strategic_verdict.reason: The current dashboard shows stronger juice/smoothie white space on Golf Links and Speedway than on Kolb Road alone. The intersection strategy captures Kolb access while using the stronger cross-corridor demand signal.

menu_rules: Launch with six core smoothies, two cold refreshers and no build-your-own menu.
Use only two cup sizes: 16 oz and 24 oz.
Keep at least 70% of ingredients shared across multiple products.
Do not launch fresh-pressed juice, a large bowl menu or a full kitchen during the first paid test.
Add bowls and one hot breakfast item only after the drink menu proves demand and speed.
Every recipe must have a weighed build card, target cost and service-time target.

zones.name: Golf Links × Kolb
zones.format: Trailer, shopping-center pad, end-cap or ground lease
zones.reason: Golf Links leads the current juice/smoothie corridor ranking and the captured dataset shows no dedicated juice/smoothie listing on the corridor.

zones.name: Speedway × Kolb
zones.format: Second-generation end-cap, pad lease or backup position on a compact drive-through site
zones.reason: Speedway combines strong review activity and zero captured dedicated juice/smoothie supply, but compact commercial land is expensive and scarce.

zones.name: 22nd × Kolb
zones.format: End-cap, inline pickup store or mobile test
zones.reason: The corridor has very strong review activity, one captured juice/smoothie competitor and meaningful breakfast demand.

zones.name: Kolb corridor alone
zones.format: Use only where a strong cross-street and practical site exist
zones.verdict: Do not choose only because it says Kolb
zones.reason: Kolb has white space, but the underlying demand signal is weaker than Golf Links and Speedway. The intersection matters more than the street name.

site_requirements: Target a 0.25–0.75 acre pad or an 800–1,200 square foot second-generation end-cap.
Require legal beverage/restaurant use and written confirmation that drive-through or pickup-window use is allowed.
Require practical ingress and egress, visibility from the arterial and room for at least 12 vehicles if using a drive-through.
Prefer shared access through a shopping center over paying to create a new curb cut.
Verify electrical capacity, water, sewer, drainage, grease-interceptor requirements and signage before signing.
Stay near gyms, schools, medical offices, apartment clusters and commuter routes, but avoid a site that is difficult to enter during peak traffic.
With a land budget under $200,000, prioritize a lease, ground lease, subdivided pad or second-generation space over raw-land ownership.

launch_plan.name: Recipe lab
launch_plan.deliverable: Six weighed smoothie recipes, two refreshers, exact food cost and 40–60 blind taste tests.

launch_plan.name: Paid corridor test
launch_plan.deliverable: Test Golf Links × Kolb and Speedway × Kolb using a permitted pop-up, shared kitchen, trailer partner or event setup.

launch_plan.name: 90-day mobile or kiosk pilot
launch_plan.deliverable: Prove repeat purchase, daypart demand, staffing, service time and a stable top-selling menu.

launch_plan.name: Second-generation store
launch_plan.deliverable: Lease an end-cap or existing food-use location. Do not make raw-land ownership a prerequisite.

pilot_targets.note: These are working validation thresholds, not guarantees or lender standards.
